title: ConfirmDialog
wrapsNative: MonarchDialog with a MonarchButton in the Danger variant as its confirm action
summary: Confirming a consequential action is a MonarchDialog whose confirm button is a danger MonarchButton and whose dismiss button is Cancel. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Before an action that deletes or cannot be undone. Say in the title what will happen and in the text what changes; name the button after the action.
whenNotToUse: Do not confirm actions that are easy to undo: do them and offer undo in a snackbar. For a choice between several options see choice-dialog; for a value see prompt-dialog.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, title: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, dismissOnClickOutside: Boolean = dismissible, paneTitle: String? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, …)

states.name: asking
states.description: The title, the consequences and two buttons: Cancel (ghost) and the action (danger).

states.name: type to confirm
states.description: A MonarchTextField as the dialog's content; the danger button is disabled until the phrase matches.

states.name: pending
states.description: The danger button is loading and back and outside taps are turned off, so the dialog stays while the action runs.

states.name: failed
states.description: The content shows the error, for example in a MonarchInlineNotice, and the button can be pressed again.

appearance: MonarchDialog in the raised background role with the default and muted text roles. The confirm button is the danger solid role with its on-solid text; Cancel is a ghost button in the default text role. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web ConfirmDialog has consequences, a confirm phrase, an acknowledgement checkbox, a reason field, and pending and error states. An Android MonarchDialog stays until the app stops composing it, so all of these fit in its slots: the consequences and fields in text, a loading MonarchButton for pending, and an error message. Material's own buttons have no danger look, so the confirm button is a MonarchButton. iOS uses the system alert, which closes when a button is tapped.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack reads the title and text when the dialog opens and stays inside it.
The danger button says the action ("Delete") so the meaning does not depend on its color.
A loading MonarchButton is announced as busy and ignores taps while the action runs.
Back calls onDismissRequest, which is Cancel, unless it is turned off while pending.
edgeCases: Do not put the danger button where a quick double tap on the opening control would hit it; MonarchDialog places it at the end, after Cancel.
The type-to-confirm phrase compares the exact text; trim or ignore case if the product allows it.
